  5552	def claim_readiness_for(
  5553	    analysis_manifest: AnalysisManifestState | None,
  5554	    collection_verdict: str,
  5555	    evaluations: list[MemberEvaluation],
  5556	) -> dict[str, Any]:
  5557	    base = {
  5558	        "verdict": "not_assessed",
  5559	        "reasons": [],
  5560	        "required_contrast_ids": [],
  5561	        "ready_contrast_ids": [],
  5562	        "not_ready_contrasts": [],
  5563	        "note": CLAIM_READINESS_NOTE,
  5564	    }
  5565	    if analysis_manifest is None:
  5566	        return base
  5567	    if not analysis_manifest.valid:
  5568	        base.update(
  5569	            {
  5570	                "verdict": "not_ready_for_analysis",
  5571	                "reasons": _manifest_readiness_reasons(analysis_manifest),
  5572	            }
  5573	        )
  5574	        return base
  5575	    contrasts = analysis_manifest.raw.get("contrasts")
  5576	    if not isinstance(contrasts, list) or not contrasts:
  5577	        return base
  5578	    required_ids = [
  5579	        contrast.get("contrast_id")
  5580	        for contrast in contrasts
  5581	        if isinstance(contrast, dict) and isinstance(contrast.get("contrast_id"), str)
  5582	    ]
  5583	    base["required_contrast_ids"] = required_ids
  5584	    entries = analysis_manifest.raw.get("entries")
  5585	    assert isinstance(entries, list)
  5586	    evaluation_by_bundle = {evaluation.bundle_id: evaluation for evaluation in evaluations}
  5587	    ready_ids: list[str] = []
  5588	    not_ready: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
  5589	    all_reasons: set[str] = set()
  5590	
  5591	    for contrast in contrasts:
  5592	        if not isinstance(contrast, dict):
  5593	            continue
  5594	        contrast_id = contrast.get("contrast_id")
  5595	        if not isinstance(contrast_id, str):
  5596	            continue
  5597	        reasons: set[str] = set()
  5598	        affected: list[str] = []
  5599	        ratio_pairs: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]] = []
  5600	        if collection_verdict != "usable":
  5601	            reasons.add("fixed_n_plan_incomplete")
  5602	        block_ids = contrast.get("block_ids")
  5603	        cell_a = contrast.get("cell_a_id")
  5604	        cell_b = contrast.get("cell_b_id")
  5605	        if not isinstance(block_ids, list) or not all(isinstance(item, str) for item in block_ids):
  5606	            reasons.add("fixed_n_plan_incomplete")
  5607	            block_ids = []
  5608	        complete_blocks = 0
  5609	        for block_id in block_ids:
  5610	            pair: list[MemberEvaluation] = []
  5611	            for cell_id in (cell_a, cell_b):
  5612	                matches = [
  5613	                    entry
  5614	                    for entry in entries
  5615	                    if isinstance(entry, dict)
  5616	                    and entry.get("block_id") == block_id
  5617	                    and entry.get("cell_id") == cell_id
  5618	                ]
  5619	                if len(matches) != 1:
  5620	                    reasons.update({"bundle_missing", "paired_block_incomplete"})
  5621	                    continue
  5622	                run_id = matches[0].get("run_id")
  5623	                evaluation = evaluation_by_bundle.get(run_id)
  5624	                if evaluation is None:
  5625	                    reasons.update({"bundle_missing", "paired_block_incomplete"})
  5626	                    if isinstance(run_id, str):
  5627	                        affected.append(run_id)
  5628	                    continue
  5629	                affected.append(evaluation.bundle_id)
  5630	                pair.append(evaluation)
  5631	                reasons.update(_member_readiness_reasons(evaluation, contrast))
  5632	            if len(pair) == 2:
  5633	                metric = contrast.get("metric")
  5634	                if isinstance(metric, dict) and metric.get("ratio_estimand") is not None:
  5635	                    ratio_pairs.append(
  5636	                        (
  5637	                            pair[0].ratio_token_provenance,
  5638	                            pair[1].ratio_token_provenance,
  5639	                        )
  5640	                    )
  5641	                    reasons.update(
  5642	                        ratio_evidence_reasons(
  5643	                            pair[0].ratio_token_provenance,
  5644	                            pair[1].ratio_token_provenance,
  5645	                        )
  5646	                    )
  5647	                complete_blocks += 1
  5648	        if ratio_pairs:
  5649	            reasons.update(ratio_collection_evidence_reasons(tuple(ratio_pairs)))
  5650	        design = analysis_manifest.raw.get("design")
  5651	        sampling_plan = design.get("sampling_plan") if isinstance(design, dict) else None
  5652	        planned_n = (
  5653	            sampling_plan.get("planned_n_blocks") if isinstance(sampling_plan, dict) else None
  5654	        )
  5655	        if (
  5656	            isinstance(planned_n, bool)
  5657	            or not isinstance(planned_n, int)
  5658	            or planned_n < 1
  5659	            or len(block_ids) != planned_n
  5660	            or complete_blocks != planned_n
  5661	        ):
  5662	            reasons.add("fixed_n_plan_incomplete")
  5663	        if reasons:
  5664	            ordered = sorted(reasons)
  5665	            all_reasons.update(ordered)
  5666	            not_ready.append(
  5667	                {
  5668	                    "contrast_id": contrast_id,
  5669	                    "affected_member_ids": sorted(set(affected)),
  5670	                    "reasons": ordered,
  5671	                }
  5672	            )
  5673	        else:
  5674	            ready_ids.append(contrast_id)
  5675	
  5676	    base.update(
  5677	        {
  5678	            "verdict": (
  5679	                "ready_for_analysis"
  5680	                if len(ready_ids) == len(required_ids) and required_ids
  5681	                else "not_ready_for_analysis"
  5682	            ),
  5683	            "reasons": sorted(all_reasons),
  5684	            "ready_contrast_ids": ready_ids,
  5685	            "not_ready_contrasts": not_ready,
  5686	        }
  5687	    )
  5688	    return base

  5691	def _idle_admission_claim_barrier_reasons(core: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
  5692	    """Map the advisory core surface onto claim-bearing refusal reasons."""
  5693	
  5694	    reasons: set[str] = set()
  5695	    conditions = core.get("conditions")
  5696	    if isinstance(conditions, list):
  5697	        for condition in (
  5698	            "environment_admission_failed",
  5699	            "instrument_calibration_bracket_missing",
  5700	            "instrument_calibration_mismatch",
  5701	            "instrument_calibration_stale",
  5702	            "thermal_pressure_elevated_in_window",
  5703	            "environment_admission_missing",
  5704	        ):
  5705	            if condition in conditions:
  5706	                reasons.add(condition)
  5707	    members = core.get("members")
  5708	    if not isinstance(members, list) or not members:
  5709	        reasons.add("cpu_admission_core_missing")
  5710	    elif any(
  5711	        not isinstance(member, Mapping)
  5712	        or not isinstance(member.get("cpu_admission"), Mapping)
  5713	        or member["cpu_admission"].get("decision") != "admitted"
  5714	        for member in members
  5715	    ):
  5716	        reasons.add("cpu_admission_core_failed")
  5717	    continuity = core.get("adapter_wattage_continuity")
  5718	    if not isinstance(continuity, Mapping):
  5719	        reasons.add("adapter_continuity_evidence_missing")
  5720	    elif continuity.get("decision") != "stable":
  5721	        reasons.add("adapter_continuity_failed")
  5722	    bracket = core.get("neg8_bracket")
  5723	    if not isinstance(bracket, Mapping) or bracket.get("decision") == "not_evaluated":
  5724	        reasons.add("whole_window_neg8_verdict_missing")
  5725	    elif bracket.get("decision") != "passed":
  5726	        reasons.add("whole_window_neg8_verdict_failed")
  5727	    return sorted(reasons)
  5728	
  5729	
  5730	def apply_idle_admission_claim_barrier(
  5731	    readiness: dict[str, Any], core: Mapping[str, Any], *, claim_bearing: bool
  5732	) -> dict[str, Any]:
  5733	    if not claim_bearing:
  5734	        return readiness
  5735	    reasons = _idle_admission_claim_barrier_reasons(core)
  5736	    if not reasons:
  5737	        return readiness
  5738	    result = dict(readiness)
  5739	    result["verdict"] = "not_ready_for_analysis"
  5740	    result["reasons"] = sorted(set(result.get("reasons", [])) | set(reasons))
  5741	    result["ready_contrast_ids"] = []
  5742	    existing = {
  5743	        row.get("contrast_id"): dict(row)
  5744	        for row in result.get("not_ready_contrasts", [])
  5745	        if isinstance(row, dict) and isinstance(row.get("contrast_id"), str)
  5746	    }
  5747	    for contrast_id in result.get("required_contrast_ids", []):
  5748	        if not isinstance(contrast_id, str):
  5749	            continue
  5750	        row = existing.setdefault(
  5751	            contrast_id,
  5752	            {
  5753	                "contrast_id": contrast_id,
  5754	                "affected_member_ids": [],
  5755	                "reasons": [],
  5756	            },
  5757	        )
  5758	        row["reasons"] = sorted(set(row.get("reasons", [])) | set(reasons))
  5759	    result["not_ready_contrasts"] = [existing[key] for key in sorted(existing)]
  5760	    return result

  5763	def sampling_audit_for(analysis_manifest: AnalysisManifestState | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
  5764	    planned_n: int | None = None
  5765	    design_name: str | None = None
  5766	    registered: list[str] = []
  5767	    if analysis_manifest is not None:
  5768	        design = analysis_manifest.raw.get("design")
  5769	        sampling = design.get("sampling_plan") if isinstance(design, dict) else None
  5770	        if isinstance(sampling, dict):
  5771	            design_name = (
  5772	                sampling.get("design")
  5773	                if isinstance(sampling.get("design"), str)
  5774	                else None
  5775	            )
  5776	            value = sampling.get("planned_n_blocks")
  5777	            planned_n = value if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) else None
  5778	        entries = analysis_manifest.raw.get("entries")
  5779	        if isinstance(entries, list):
  5780	            registered = sorted(
  5781	                entry["run_id"]
  5782	                for entry in entries
  5783	                if isinstance(entry, dict) and isinstance(entry.get("run_id"), str)
  5784	            )
  5785	    return {
  5786	        "design": design_name,
  5787	        "planned_n_blocks": planned_n,
  5788	        "registered_bundle_ids": registered,
  5789	        "unregistered_matching_bundle_ids": [],
  5790	        "valid_replacements": [],
  5791	        "top_up_suspected": False,

  5795	def print_verdict(
  5796	    collection_verdict: str,
  5797	    collection_reasons: list[str],
  5798	    categories: dict[str, list[str]],
  5799	    claim_readiness: dict[str, Any],
  5800	) -> None:
  5801	    print("COLLECTION VERDICT:")
  5802	    print(f"  verdict: {collection_verdict}")
  5803	    for reason in collection_reasons:

    43	def evaluate_environment_policy(
    44	    snapshot: Mapping[str, Any],
    45	    policy: EnvironmentGuardPolicy | None = None,
    46	) -> dict[str, Any]:
    47	    """Purely evaluate one captured snapshot against the quiet-host policy.
    48	
    49	    Doctor and the campaign runner share this evaluator.  The former renders
    50	    the result as advisory evidence; the latter enforces ``eligible``.  Load
    51	    average is copied as evidence only and is deliberately absent from the
    52	    finding predicates.
    53	    """
    54	
    55	    selected = policy if policy is not None else EnvironmentGuardPolicy()
    56	    power = snapshot.get("power")
    57	    external_connected = (
    58	        power.get("external_connected") if isinstance(power, Mapping) else None
    59	    )
    60	    checks = (
    61	        (
    62	            selected.require_ac_power,
    63	            "power_source_not_ac",
    64	            "power_source",
    65	            snapshot.get("power_source"),
    66	            "AC Power",
    67	        ),
    68	        (
    69	            selected.require_external_connected,
    70	            "external_power_not_connected",
    71	            "power.external_connected",
    72	            external_connected,
    73	            True,
    74	        ),
    75	        (
    76	            selected.require_low_power_mode_off,
    77	            "low_power_mode_enabled",
    78	            "low_power_mode",
    79	            snapshot.get("low_power_mode"),
    80	            False,
    81	        ),
    82	        (
    83	            selected.require_displays_asleep,
    84	            "display_not_all_asleep",
    85	            "display_power_state",
    86	            snapshot.get("display_power_state"),
    87	            "all_asleep",
    88	        ),
    89	        (
    90	            selected.require_screensaver_disengaged,
    91	            "screensaver_engaged",
    92	            "screensaver_engaged",
    93	            snapshot.get("screensaver_engaged"),
    94	            False,
    95	        ),
    96	        (
    97	            selected.require_thermal_nominal,
    98	            "thermal_not_nominal",
    99	            "thermal_pressure",
   100	            snapshot.get("thermal_pressure"),
   101	            "nominal",
   102	        ),
   103	    )
   104	    findings: list[EnvironmentFinding] = []
   105	    for enabled, code, field, actual, required in checks:
   106	        if not enabled:
   107	            continue
   108	        comparable_actual = actual.lower() if isinstance(actual, str) else actual
   109	        comparable_required = required.lower() if isinstance(required, str) else required
   110	        if actual is None:
   111	            status = "unknown"
   112	        elif comparable_actual == comparable_required:
   113	            status = "pass"
   114	        else:
   115	            status = "fail"
   116	        findings.append(
   117	            EnvironmentFinding(
   118	                code=code,
   119	                field=field,
   120	                status=status,
   121	                actual=actual,
   122	                required=required,
   123	            )
   124	        )
   125	    serialized_findings = [finding.to_dict() for finding in findings]
   126	    blocked = any(finding.status == "fail" for finding in findings) or (
   127	        selected.critical_unknown_fail_closed
   128	        and any(finding.status == "unknown" for finding in findings)
   129	    )
   130	    snapshot_value = dict(snapshot)
   131	    return {
   132	        "schema_version": "joulewise.environment_evaluation.v1",
   133	        "eligible": not blocked,
   134	        "findings": serialized_findings,
   135	        "snapshot_sha256": _canonical_sha256(snapshot_value),
   136	        "findings_sha256": _canonical_sha256(serialized_findings),
   137	        "load_average_evidence": {
   138	            "load_average_1m": snapshot.get("load_average_1m"),
   139	            "load_average_5m": snapshot.get("load_average_5m"),
   140	            "load_average_15m": snapshot.get("load_average_15m"),
   141	            "admission_gate": False,
   142	        },
   143	    }

   146	def probe_thermal_pressure(
   147	    timeout_s: float = COMMAND_TIMEOUT_S,
   148	) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
   149	    """Return macOS thermal pressure from the read-only ``pmset`` probe.
   150	
   151	    ``pmset -g therm`` does not require sudo.  The stable nominal sentence is
   152	    mapped to ``nominal``; other platform output is retained as ``elevated``
   153	    only when it reports an active warning/limit.  Unknown formats fail soft.
   154	    """
   155	    stdout, error = _run(["pmset", "-g", "therm"], timeout_s)
   156	    if stdout is None:
   157	        return None, error
   158	    normalized = " ".join(stdout.lower().split())
   159	    if "no thermal warning level has been recorded" in normalized:
   160	        return "nominal", None
   161	    limits = [
   162	        int(value)
   163	        for value in re.findall(
   164	            r"(?:speed|scheduler)_limit\s*=\s*(\d+)", normalized
   165	        )
   166	    ]
   167	    if limits:
   168	        return ("elevated" if any(value < 100 for value in limits) else "nominal"), None
   169	    if "thermal warning" in normalized or "thermal level" in normalized:
   170	        return "elevated", None
   171	    return None, "unrecognized_output"

   243	def collect_environment_snapshot(timeout_s: float = COMMAND_TIMEOUT_S) -> dict[str, Any]:
   244	    """Return a best-effort machine-wide environment snapshot.
   245	
   246	    Every subprocess is sudo-free and independently optional: missing commands,
   247	    nonzero exits, timeouts, and parse failures leave that command's fields as
   248	    ``None`` and add a terse entry to ``errors``. This function never raises.
   249	
   250	    ``memory_pressure_percent`` is derived from a free-memory percentage when
   251	    available; it is a pressure proxy, not the kernel's memorystatus level.
   252	    """
   253	    snapshot: dict[str, Any] = empty_environment_snapshot()
   254	    errors: dict[str, str] = {}
   255	
   256	    _apply_command(
   257	        snapshot,
   258	        errors,
   259	        "pmset_batt",
   260	        ["pmset", "-g", "batt"],
   261	        _parse_pmset_batt,
   262	        timeout_s,

   264	    _apply_command(

   280	    memory_ok = _apply_command(

   288	    if not memory_ok:

    68	def _attempt_capture_interval(
    69	    bundle_path: Path, attempt: int

    71	    """Read the producer's endpoint-stamped idle telemetry interval."""

   102	            # Untimestamped legacy diagnostics remain replayable because

   104	            return None

   112	        return None
   113	    return min(starts), max(ends)

   525	def _package_version_record(distribution: str) -> dict[str, str | bool | None]:

   535	def _apply_command(
   536	    snapshot: dict[str, Any],
   537	    errors: dict[str, str],
   538	    key: str,
   539	    command: list[str],
   540	    parser,
   541	    timeout_s: float,
   542	) -> bool:
   543	    stdout, error = _run(command, timeout_s)
   544	    if stdout is None:
   545	        errors[key] = error or "failed"
   546	        return False
   547	    try:
   548	        parser(snapshot, stdout)
   549	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - snapshot collection must never raise
   550	        errors[key] = "parse"
   551	        return False
   552	    return True

   554	
   555	def _run(command: list[str], timeout_s: float) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
   556	    try:
   557	        completed = subprocess.run(
   558	            command,
   559	            capture_output=True,
   560	            text=True,
   561	            timeout=timeout_s,
   562	            check=False,
   563	        )
   564	    except FileNotFoundError:
   565	        return None, "not_found"
   566	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
   567	        return None, "timeout"
   568	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - snapshot collection must never raise
   569	        return None, "failed"
   570	    if (
   571	        completed.returncode != 0
   572	        and command
   573	        == ["defaults", "-currentHost", "read", "com.apple.screensaver"]
   574	        and "does not exist" in f"{completed.stdout}\n{completed.stderr}".lower()
   575	    ):
   576	        # A missing per-host screensaver domain is the normal macOS-default
   577	        # state, not a failed probe.  Parsing an empty domain applies the
   578	        # platform's 20-minute default while leaving engagement to HID evidence.
   579	        return "{}", None
   580	    if completed.returncode != 0:
   581	        return None, f"returncode_{completed.returncode}"
   582	    return completed.stdout, None

   585	def _parse_pmset_batt(snapshot: dict[str, Any], text: str) -> None:
   586	    source = re.search(r"Now drawing from '([^']+)'", text)
   587	    percent = re.search(r"(\d+)%", text)
   588	    state = re.search(r"\d+%;\s*([^;]+);", text)
   589	    if not source and not percent and not state:
   590	        raise ValueError("battery status not found")
   591	    if source:
   592	        snapshot["power_source"] = source.group(1)
   593	    if percent:
   594	        snapshot["battery_percent"] = int(percent.group(1))
   595	    if state:
   596	        snapshot["battery_state"] = state.group(1).strip()
   597	
   598	
   599	def _parse_pmset(snapshot: dict[str, Any], text: str) -> None:
   600	    # Missing lowpowermode is legitimate on some macOS/hardware combinations.
   601	    match = re.search(r"^\s*lowpowermode\s+([01])\s*$", text, re.MULTILINE)
   602	    if match:
   603	        snapshot["low_power_mode"] = match.group(1) == "1"
   604	        return
   605	    # Newer macOS reports the tri-state energy mode as `powermode`
   606	    # (0 automatic, 1 low power, 2 high power); only 1 is low power.
   607	    # Live-validated 2026-07-18 on macOS 26.5 (Mac15,9): `powermode 0`.
   608	    match = re.search(r"^\s*powermode\s+([012])\s*$", text, re.MULTILINE)
   609	    if match:
   610	        snapshot["low_power_mode"] = match.group(1) == "1"
   880	    ):
   881	        value = _ioreg_bool(text, raw_key)
   882	        if value is not None:
   883	            power[out_key] = value
   884	    if not any(value is not None for value in power.values()):
   885	        raise ValueError("battery power details not found")
   886	
   887	
   888	def _ioreg_bool(text: str, key: str) -> bool | None:
   889	    match = re.search(rf'"{re.escape(key)}"\s*=\s*(Yes|No|True|False)', text)
   890	    if not match:
   891	        return None
   892	    return match.group(1) in {"Yes", "True"}
   893	
   894	
   895	def _parse_kern_boottime(snapshot: dict[str, Any], text: str) -> None:
   896	    match = re.search(r"sec\s*=\s*(\d+)", text)
   897	    if not match:
   898	        raise ValueError("kern.boottime sec not found")
   899	    boot_time_s = int(match.group(1))
   900	    snapshot["boot_time_s"] = boot_time_s
   901	    snapshot["uptime_s"] = max(0.0, time.time() - boot_time_s)

   907	    clock_sync = snapshot["clock_sync"]

   916	        )
   917	    except FileNotFoundError:
   918	        clock_sync["timed_running"] = False
   919	        clock_sync["timed_probe_error"] = "not_found"
   920	        errors["pgrep_timed"] = "not_found"
   921	        return
   922	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
   923	        clock_sync["timed_running"] = False
   924	        clock_sync["timed_probe_error"] = "timeout"
   925	        errors["pgrep_timed"] = "timeout"

   927	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - snapshot collection must never raise
   928	        clock_sync["timed_running"] = False
   929	        clock_sync["timed_probe_error"] = "failed"
   930	        errors["pgrep_timed"] = "failed"
   931	        return
   932	    if completed.returncode == 0:
   933	        clock_sync["timed_running"] = True
   934	        return
   935	    clock_sync["timed_running"] = False
   936	    if completed.returncode != 1:
   937	        reason = f"returncode_{completed.returncode}"
   938	        clock_sync["timed_probe_error"] = reason
   939	        errors["pgrep_timed"] = reason

    91	class FakeClock:
    92	    """Simulated time starting at ``start``; ``sleep`` advances instantly."""
    93	
    94	    def __init__(self, start: float = 0.0) -> None:
    95	        self._start = float(start)
    96	        self._now = float(start)

    98	    def now(self) -> float:
    99	        return self._now
   100	
   101	    def stamp(self) -> ClockStamp:
   102	        return ClockStamp(
   103	            epoch_s=self._now,
   104	            monotonic_before_s=self._now,
   105	            monotonic_after_s=self._now,
   106	            wall_resolution_s=0.0,
   107	            monotonic_resolution_s=0.0,
   108	        )
   109	
   110	    def sleep(self, seconds: float) -> None:
   111	        if not is_finite_number(seconds):
   112	            raise ValueError("sleep duration must be a finite number")
   113	        if seconds < 0:
   114	            raise ValueError("cannot sleep a negative duration")
   115	        self._now += seconds
   116	
   117	    def info(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
   118	        return {"kind": "fake", "start_s": self._start}

   358	    def start_sampling(
   359	        self, config: BenchmarkConfig, context: RunContext | None = None
   360	    ) -> AdapterResult:
   361	        capability = self._ensure_capability()
   362	        if not capability.ok:
   363	            return capability
   364	        if self._process is not None:
   365	            if self._admission_sampling_handoff_pending:
   366	                if self._process.poll() is not None:
   367	                    self._reset_admission_sampling_state()
   368	                    return AdapterResult(
   369	                        ok=False,
   370	                        failure_reason=FailureReason.TELEMETRY_UNAVAILABLE,
   371	                        message=(
   372	                            "powermetrics sampling ended before the measured-window "
   373	                            "handoff"
   374	                        ),
   375	                    )
   376	                self._admission_sampling_handoff_pending = False
   377	                return AdapterResult(
   378	                    ok=True,
   379	                    metadata=dict(self._admission_sampling_metadata or {}),
   380	                )
   381	            return AdapterResult(
   382	                ok=False,
   383	                failure_reason=FailureReason.UNKNOWN_ERROR,
   384	                message="powermetrics sampling is already active",
   385	            )
   386	
   387	        self._capture_path = self._new_capture_path()
   388	        self._pending_captures[RAW_SAMPLES_NAME] = self._capture_path
   389	        self._initialize_stream_cursor(self._capture_path)
   390	        self._pre_spawn_stamp = None
   391	        self._first_parse_stamp = None
   392	        command = self._command(
   393	            config,
   394	            self._capture_path,
   395	            count=None,
   396	            interval_ms=self._interval_ms(config),
   397	        )
   398	        pre_spawn_stamp = self._clock.stamp()
   399	        self._pre_spawn_stamp = pre_spawn_stamp
   400	        try:
   401	            self._process = subprocess.Popen(
   402	                command,
   403	                stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
   404	                stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
   405	            )
   406	        except FileNotFoundError as exc:
   407	            self._release_capture(RAW_SAMPLES_NAME)
   408	            return AdapterResult(
   409	                ok=False,
   410	                failure_reason=FailureReason.TELEMETRY_UNAVAILABLE,
   411	                message=f"powermetrics launcher unavailable: {exc}",
   412	            )
   413	        ready = self._wait_until_ready(self._process, self._capture_path)
   414	        if not ready.ok:
   415	            self._stop_process(self._process)
   416	            self._process = None
   417	            self._reset_admission_sampling_state()
   418	            if context is None:
   419	                self._release_capture(RAW_SAMPLES_NAME)
   420	            return ready
   421	        if self._first_parse_stamp is None:
   422	            self._stop_process(self._process)
   423	            self._process = None
   424	            self._reset_admission_sampling_state()
   425	            return AdapterResult(
   426	                ok=False,
   427	                failure_reason=FailureReason.UNKNOWN_ERROR,
   428	                message="powermetrics readiness completed without a paired clock stamp",
   429	            )
   430	        rollover = self._wait_for_native_rollover(self._process, self._capture_path)
   431	        if not rollover.ok:
   432	            self._stop_process(self._process)
   433	            self._process = None
   434	            self._reset_admission_sampling_state()
   435	            if context is None:
   436	                self._release_capture(RAW_SAMPLES_NAME)
   437	            return rollover
   438	        self._clock_start_s = self._first_parse_stamp.epoch_s
   439	        result = AdapterResult(
   440	            ok=True,
   441	            metadata={
   442	                "command": command,
   443	                "raw_artifact": RAW_SAMPLES_NAME,
   444	                "timestamp_derivation": TIMESTAMP_DERIVATION,
   445	                "readiness": ready.metadata,
   446	                "native_rollover": rollover.metadata,
   447	            },
   448	        )
   449	        self._admission_sampling_metadata = dict(result.metadata)
   450	        return result

   452	    def begin_admission_window_sampling(
   453	        self, config: BenchmarkConfig, context: RunContext | None = None
   454	    ) -> AdapterResult:
   455	        """Start the sole sampler before the first idle-admission capture.
   456	
   457	        Admission baselines are logical, byte-verbatim slices of this stream;
   458	        the same process remains live through measured-window handoff.
   459	        """
   460	
   461	        capability = self._ensure_capability()
   462	        if not capability.ok:
   463	            return capability
   464	        if self._process is not None or self._admission_sampling_start_requested:
   465	            return AdapterResult(
   466	                ok=False,
   467	                failure_reason=FailureReason.UNKNOWN_ERROR,
   468	                message="powermetrics admission-window sampling is already active",
   469	            )
   470	        self._admission_sampling_start_requested = True
   471	        try:
   472	            result = self.start_sampling(config, context)
   473	        finally:
   474	            # An interrupt can land after native process creation but before
   475	            # ``start_sampling`` returns.  Controller finalization owns that
   476	            # process; this transient guard must never leak into adapter reuse.
   477	            self._admission_sampling_start_requested = False
   478	        if not result.ok:
   479	            self._reset_admission_sampling_state()
   480	            return result
   481	        self._admission_sampling_handoff_pending = True
   482	        return result
   483	
   484	    def stop_sampling(
   485	        self, config: BenchmarkConfig, context: RunContext | None = None
   486	    ) -> list[PowerSample]:
   487	        """Compatibility stop path used by non-controller callers and legacy tests."""
   488	
   489	        data, clock_start_s = self._take_measured_capture()
   490	        if data is None:
   491	            self._release_capture(RAW_SAMPLES_NAME)
   492	            return []
   493	        if context is not None:
   494	            self._persist_capture(context, RAW_SAMPLES_NAME, data)
   495	        records, diagnostic = _parse_powermetrics_records(
   496	            data, timestamp_anchor_s=clock_start_s
   497	        )
   498	        self._preserve_measured_capture(data, records, diagnostic, context)
   499	        self._release_capture(RAW_SAMPLES_NAME)
   500	        return samples_from_records(records)

   502	    def stop_sampling_with_evidence(
   503	        self,
   504	        config: BenchmarkConfig,
   505	        context: RunContext | None,
   506	        *,
   507	        sampling_started: ClockStamp,
   508	        sampling_stopped: ClockStamp,
   509	        required_post_window_tail_s: float = 0.0,
   510	    ) -> TelemetryStopResult:
   511	        """Stop the real sampler and derive current-era clock/phase evidence."""
   512	
   513	        bracket_deadline: float | None = None
   514	        try:
   515	            bracket_deadline = self._drain_until_stop_bracket(
   516	                config,
   517	                sampling_started=sampling_started,
   518	                sampling_stopped=sampling_stopped,
   519	                required_post_window_tail_s=required_post_window_tail_s,
   520	            )
   521	        finally:
   522	            data, _ = self._take_measured_capture()
   523	        if data is None:
   524	            self._release_capture(RAW_SAMPLES_NAME)
   525	            evidence, _ = derive_powermetrics_clock_evidence_v2(
   526	                stamps={}, records=[]
   527	            )
   528	            return TelemetryStopResult([], evidence)
   529	        native_records, diagnostic = _parse_powermetrics_records(data)
   530	        post_parse_stamp = self._clock.stamp()
   531	        stamps: dict[str, ClockStamp] = {
   532	            "sampling_started": sampling_started,
   533	            "sampling_stopped": sampling_stopped,
   534	            "post_parse": post_parse_stamp,
   535	        }
   536	        if self._pre_spawn_stamp is not None:
   537	            stamps["pre_spawn"] = self._pre_spawn_stamp
   538	        if self._first_parse_stamp is not None:
   539	            stamps["first_parse"] = self._first_parse_stamp
   540	        evidence, point_anchor_s = derive_powermetrics_clock_evidence_v2(
   541	            stamps=stamps,
   542	            records=anchor_records_from_powermetrics(native_records),
   543	        )
   544	        if bracket_deadline is not None and point_anchor_s is not None:
   545	            # Freeze only after termination and the authoritative post-parse
   546	            # stamp. The prefix must retain a record that brackets the stop
   547	            # marker under the EARLIEST allowed anchor, so the cutoff uses the
   548	            # admissible interval's lower endpoint, never the midpoint.
   549	            bracketed_data = self._freeze_stop_bracketing_prefix(
   550	                data,
   551	                native_records=native_records,
   552	                diagnostic=diagnostic,
   553	                earliest_anchor_s=float(
   554	                    evidence["clock_anchor"]["admissible_lower_epoch_s"]
   555	                ),
   556	                sampling_stopped=sampling_stopped,
   557	                deadline=bracket_deadline,
   558	                required_post_window_tail_s=required_post_window_tail_s,
   559	            )
   560	            if bracketed_data is not None:
   561	                data = bracketed_data
   562	                native_records, diagnostic = _parse_powermetrics_records(data)
   563	                evidence, point_anchor_s = derive_powermetrics_clock_evidence_v2(
   564	                    stamps=stamps,
   565	                    records=anchor_records_from_powermetrics(native_records),
   566	                )
   567	        if context is not None:
   568	            self._persist_capture(context, RAW_SAMPLES_NAME, data)
   569	        # Fail-closed timeline: an unresolved anchor (clock_anchor_unresolved)
   570	        # still needs a structurally valid, window-overlapping trace layout.
   571	        # The claim barrier lives in the evidence - the fallback endpoint is
   572	        # recorded there so strict raw-to-trace re-derivation replays it, and
   573	        # it never re-enters any claim math.
   574	        trace_endpoint_s = point_anchor_s
   575	        if trace_endpoint_s is None and native_records:
   576	            trace_endpoint_s, fallback_method = trace_fallback_endpoint(
   577	                stamps, native_records
   578	            )
   579	            clock_anchor = evidence.get("clock_anchor")
   580	            if isinstance(clock_anchor, dict):
   581	                clock_anchor["trace_fallback_endpoint_epoch_s"] = trace_endpoint_s
   582	                clock_anchor["trace_fallback_method"] = fallback_method
   583	        records = (
   584	            parse_powermetrics_records(data, first_record_endpoint_s=trace_endpoint_s)
   585	            if trace_endpoint_s is not None
   586	            else native_records
   587	        )
   588	        self._preserve_measured_capture(
   589	            data,
   590	            records,
   591	            diagnostic,
   592	            context,
   593	            first_record_endpoint_s=trace_endpoint_s,
   594	        )
   595	        self._release_capture(RAW_SAMPLES_NAME)
   596	        return TelemetryStopResult(samples_from_records(records), evidence)

   598	    def _drain_until_stop_bracket(
   599	        self,
   600	        config: BenchmarkConfig,
   601	        *,
   602	        sampling_started: ClockStamp,
   603	        sampling_stopped: ClockStamp,
   604	        required_post_window_tail_s: float = 0.0,
   605	    ) -> float | None:
   606	        """Bound sampler wind-down by a trace-domain right-edge sample."""
   607	
   608	        process = self._process
   609	        capture_path = self._capture_path
   610	        if process is None or capture_path is None:
   611	            return None
   612	        drain_started_s = self._drain_monotonic()
   613	        anchor_lag_s = self._measured_anchor_lag_s(
   614	            sampling_started=sampling_started,
   615	            sampling_stopped=sampling_stopped,
   616	        )
   617	        timeout_s = (
   618	            anchor_lag_s
   619	            + 2.0 / config.sampling.power_hz
   620	            + POST_MARKER_DRAIN_MARGIN_S
   621	        )
   622	        deadline = drain_started_s + timeout_s
   623	        while self._drain_monotonic() < deadline and process.poll() is None:
   624	            brackets_stop = self._capture_brackets_stop(
   625	                capture_path,
   626	                deadline=deadline,
   627	                sampling_started=sampling_started,
   628	                sampling_stopped=sampling_stopped,
   629	                required_post_window_tail_s=required_post_window_tail_s,
   630	            )
   631	            if brackets_stop:
   632	                return deadline
   633	            remaining_s = deadline - self._drain_monotonic()
   634	            if remaining_s <= 0.0:
   635	                return None
   636	            # This wait is after the sampling_stopped marker. It only lets the
   637	            # native stream provide the right-edge interval; reducer windows
   638	            # remain marker-bounded and exclude support after that timestamp.
   639	            self._drain_sleep(min(POST_MARKER_DRAIN_POLL_S, remaining_s))
   640	        return None
   641	
   642	    def _measured_anchor_lag_s(
   643	        self,
   644	        *,
   645	        sampling_started: ClockStamp,
   646	        sampling_stopped: ClockStamp,
   647	    ) -> float:
   648	        """Return the provisional midpoint-anchor lag used by trace timestamps."""
   649	
   650	        pre_spawn = self._pre_spawn_stamp
   651	        first_parse = self._first_parse_stamp
   652	        if pre_spawn is None or first_parse is None:
   653	            return 0.0
   654	        stamps = (
   655	            pre_spawn,
   656	            first_parse,
   657	            sampling_started,
   658	            sampling_stopped,
   659	            # Match the provisional drain anchor: the authoritative post-parse
   660	            # stamp does not exist until after sampler termination.
   661	            sampling_stopped,
   662	        )
   663	        values = (
   664	            value
   665	            for stamp in stamps
   666	            for value in (
   667	                stamp.epoch_s,
   668	                stamp.monotonic_before_s,
   669	                stamp.monotonic_after_s,
   670	                stamp.wall_resolution_s,
   671	                stamp.monotonic_resolution_s,
   672	            )
   673	        )
   674	        if not all(math.isfinite(value) for value in values):
   675	            return 0.0
   676	        if any(
   677	            stamp.monotonic_before_s > stamp.monotonic_after_s
   678	            or stamp.wall_resolution_s < 0.0
   679	            or stamp.monotonic_resolution_s < 0.0
   680	            for stamp in stamps
   681	        ):
   682	            return 0.0
   683	
   684	        offset_lowers_s: list[float] = []
   685	        offset_uppers_s: list[float] = []
   686	        for stamp in stamps:
   687	            resolution_s = max(
   688	                stamp.wall_resolution_s,
   689	                stamp.monotonic_resolution_s,
   690	            )
   691	            offset_lowers_s.append(
   692	                stamp.epoch_s - stamp.monotonic_after_s - resolution_s
   693	            )
   694	            offset_uppers_s.append(
   695	                stamp.epoch_s - stamp.monotonic_before_s + resolution_s
   696	            )
   697	        first_endpoint_lower_s = (
   698	            pre_spawn.monotonic_before_s + min(offset_lowers_s)
   699	        )

title="docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>measurement_methodology.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 6d80039</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Measurement Methodology</h1> <p>Living cross-phase contract, drafted in Phase 1. Changes require a decision-log entry when they bind later work.</p> <h2 id="measurement-principle">Measurement Principle</h2> <p>Every benchmark run must be reproducible from its raw artifacts. Summary metrics are derived outputs, not the source of truth.</p> <p>The source of truth for a run is the run bundle:</p> <ul> <li>Experiment config.</li> <li>Device and environment metadata.</li> <li>Event log with phase timestamps.</li> <li>Raw power trace.</li> <li>Raw model output.</li> <li>Reducer output.</li> <li>Runtime and telemetry logs.</li> </ul> <h2 id="run-lifecycle">Run Lifecycle</h2> <p>Before a campaign creates a run bundle, the operator runs the read-only doctor preflight described in <code>docs/contracts/doctor_preflight.md</code>. Schema-0.1 parsing continues to warn-and-ignore unknown keys for compatibility, but campaign execution fails before the first bundle when those warnings have not been explicitly acknowledged. The terminal campaign-verdict JSONL row records the exact warning set and acknowledgement; acknowledgement does not alter config bytes, collection evidence, claim readiness, or claim outcomes.</p> <p>Doctor also exposes architecture/version, configured model and tokenizer identity, requested sampler fields, inspect-only powermetrics privilege policy, thermal pressure, backup capacity, and quiet-machine warnings. These are preflight observations, not substitutes for per-bundle provenance or live measurement gates. In particular, doctor never starts powermetrics and never certifies that a machine is quiet.</p> <h3>Environment guard and per-run admission (D-077)</h3> <p>Campaigns select a strictly typed policy sidecar. <code>run_campaign.py</code> defaults to <code>configs/campaign_policies/quiet_mac_p2_production.json</code>, records the policy version and exact source-byte SHA-256 in campaign provenance and every member bundle, acquires the campaign lock, and only then performs the enforcing environment preflight before member 1. The production quiet-Mac guard requires AC power and an externally connected power source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Unknown critical probes fail closed. Load averages are recorded as preflight evidence only and never gate a member.</p> <p>Default operation is verify-only. <code>--arm-quiet-mode</code> is an explicit transient operation: the runner displays a countdown, requests <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, and repeats the complete environment probe before deciding admission. It does not write display-sleep, screensaver, or other persistent host settings. An operator override is accepted only when its JSON binds the exact failed snapshot and findings SHA-256 values and records a reason, approver, and timestamp. It is stored as an <code>override</code>, not a waiver, and universally bars all resulting members from gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</p> <p>At each governed member&#39;s idle-baseline stage, the controller captures the same critical environment evidence and verifies that the display remains asleep and the screensaver remains disengaged. Awake, engaged, or unknown state aborts immediately. The first idle baseline is admitted only when the existing powermetrics GPU-idle-quality classification records <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code>. One and only one complete retry is allowed; both attempts preserve distinct raw artifacts and provenance. A persistent failure either aborts (production) or records the exploratory-only, unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> claim barrier (<code>on_fail: flag</code>). There is no skip disposition in a fixed-n campaign. A lightweight post-run display/screensaver/HID observation makes within-member transitions visible.</p> <p>The sidecar is deliberately separate from <code>BenchmarkConfig</code>. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy flag-only/non-enforcing behavior, and omission of the additive policy/admission metadata preserves legacy normalized config serialization and hashes.</p> <h3>Per-bundle source provenance</h3> <p><code>RunBundleWriter.create</code> captures the harness source state before it creates bundle artifacts or returns control to any adapter. <code>write_metadata</code> captures the end state after adapter execution. <code>metadata.git_commit</code> remains the creation-time commit for compatibility; the governed record is <code>metadata.source_provenance</code> with schema <code>joulewise.source_provenance.v1</code>.</p> <p>Each <code>start</code> and <code>end</code> snapshot records <code>git_commit</code>, <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, <code>untracked</code>, and <code>diff_sha256</code>. The three state values are independently:</p> <ul> <li><code>clean</code>: the corresponding Git probe succeeded and found no change;</li> <li><code>dirty</code>: an unstaged tracked diff, staged diff, or non-ignored untracked path was present, respectively; or</li> <li><code>unknown</code>: the corresponding probe or required file read failed. Failure is never interpreted as clean.</li> </ul> <p>The privacy-safe diff identity descriptor is <code>sha256</code> / <code>joulewise.git-diff.nul-v1</code>. The producer captures the byte output of <code>git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --binary</code>, the analogous <code>--cached</code> command, and <code>git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z</code>. For each sorted untracked path it hashes, without serializing, the NUL-safe length-framed path, file kind, mode, size, and SHA-256 of regular-file bytes or symlink-target bytes. The final identity is SHA-256 over the version plus length-framed <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, and untracked-inventory byte identities. Bundles contain only the final digest and state labels: never a diff, path, untracked file content, or secret.</p> <p><code>changed_during_run</code> is true when two fully known snapshots differ, false when they match, and null when either snapshot is not fully known. <code>claim_eligible</code> is true only when both commits and diff identities are known, all six component states are clean, and the snapshots match. <code>reason_codes</code> is the deterministic list of every start/end unknown or dirty component followed, when applicable, by <code>source_changed_during_run</code>. Bundle completion remains allowed in every state so raw evidence is not discarded.</p> <p>Dirty, unknown, changed, missing, or internally inconsistent provenance is a hard exclusion for claim-bearing use. The publication pack preflight enforces that boundary and refuses such bundles. Analysis-side admission propagation is separate from capture and field semantics and is owned by WO-004/T11.</p> <ol> <li>Validate config.</li> <li>Create run directory.</li> <li>Collect device metadata.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Warm up runtime.</li> <li>Wait the configured post-warmup settling interval (<code>sampling.warmup_seconds</code>; zero means no wait).</li> <li>Start measured telemetry.</li> <li>Run workload.</li> <li>Stop measured telemetry.</li> <li>Cleanup runtime.</li> <li>Reduce raw artifacts into summary metrics.</li> </ol> <p>The post-warmup settling interval begins only after all active <code>workload_profile.warmup_runs</code> calls and their clock-alignment captures have completed. It ends before the measured-run stage and sampling-active markers, so it is never integrated into the measured window. Controller events record the configured value on the warmup completion event and the runtime log records positive waits.</p> <h2 id="idle-subtraction">Idle Subtraction</h2> <p>Energy metrics must report both gross and idle-subtracted values when possible. The idle baseline is measured before each run and stored in the run bundle.</p> <p>Minimum idle fields:</p> <ul> <li><code>idle_power_w_mean</code></li> <li><code>idle_power_w_stddev</code></li> <li><code>idle_duration_s</code></li> <li><code>idle_sample_count</code></li> <li><code>telemetry_backend</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="thermal-state">Thermal State</h2> <p>Each telemetry backend should report thermal state before and after measured runs when the platform exposes it.</p> <p>Minimum thermal fields:</p> <ul> <li><code>temperature_c</code></li> <li><code>thermal_pressure</code> or platform equivalent, when available.</li> <li><code>fan_state</code> or cooling mode, when available.</li> </ul> <h2 id="uncertainty">Uncertainty</h2> <p>Phase 1 defines uncertainty fields; Phase 2 implements reducer behavior. Repeated runs should report:</p> <ul> <li>Number of repetitions.</li> <li>Mean.</li> <li>Standard deviation.</li> <li>Confidence interval method.</li> <li>Confidence interval bounds.</li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-quality-fields">Measurement Quality Fields</h2> <p>Each run summary should include:</p> <ul> <li>Sampling rate requested.</li> <li>Sampling rate observed.</li> <li>Dropped or malformed samples.</li> <li>Idle variance.</li> <li>Thermal drift.</li> <li>Telemetry source.</li> <li>Local runtime cleanup result (<code>runtime_cleanup_ok</code>: true/false/null). Cleanup occurs after the measured window, so failure is a quality concern for the following repetition and does not retroactively change current-run status or energy.</li> <li>Wall-meter comparison delta, when available.</li> </ul> <h2 id="phase-labels">Phase Labels</h2> <p>The event log should use stable phase names:</p> <ul> <li><code>idle</code></li> <li><code>warmup</code></li> <li><code>prefill</code></li> <li><code>decode</code></li> <li><code>serialize</code></li> <li><code>transfer</code></li> <li><code>deserialize</code></li> <li><code>cleanup</code></li> <li><code>failure</code></li> </ul> <p><code>deserialize</code> (cache load on the decode node) was added 2026-06-09 alongside the split-run accounting definitions (see <code>docs/phase_3/phase_3_plan.md</code>); phase labels are strings in the schema, so the addition is non-breaking. Split-stage accounting, pinned so reducers and prose agree: serialize = cache-persist window on the prefill node; transfer = byte-movement window; deserialize = cache-load window on the decode node; decode = first-token to last-token. Cache load is not decode energy.</p> <h2 id="hardware-classification">Hardware Classification</h2> <p>Every target should end Phase 1 in one state:</p> <ul> <li><code>supported</code>: known viable and ready for Phase 2 implementation.</li> <li><code>pending</code>: expected viable but not fully checked.</li> <li><code>unsupported</code>: not viable for a documented technical reason.</li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-boundaries">Measurement Boundaries</h2> <p>&quot;Power&quot; means a different physical boundary on each telemetry backend. Cross-target absolute comparisons must state the boundary difference; the final report&#39;s limitations section inherits this table. Decision D-018 defines the rail policy (per-rail trace rows plus a per-backend rail manifest naming the canonical sum).</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Backend</th> <th>Boundary</th> <th>Included</th> <th>Excluded</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>powermetrics</td> <td>Apple SoC subsystems</td> <td>CPU + GPU + ANE package power</td> <td>display, storage, memory at wall, PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>nvidia_smi</td> <td>GPU board</td> <td>board power as reported by driver</td> <td>host CPU, DRAM, motherboard, PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>jetson_rails</td> <td>module input (VDD_IN preferred; actual rail recorded)</td> <td>module power</td> <td>carrier-board peripherals (rail-dependent), PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>wall_meter</td> <td>full system AC</td> <td>everything incl. PSU losses</td> <td>nothing</td> </tr> <tr> <td>mock</td> <td>synthetic</td> <td>n/a</td> <td>n/a</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Rules:</p> <ul> <li>Within-target comparisons (the same backend) are always boundary-consistent and are the primary claim type.</li> <li>Cross-target comparisons are reported with boundaries named; where the wall meter exists, the wall-vs-platform delta is recorded per target and used to contextualize the gap.</li> <li>Each telemetry adapter declares its rail manifest in <code>device_metadata</code>; the reducer sums exactly the manifest rails to produce <code>power_w</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="clock-synchronization-and-multi-node-alignment">Clock Synchronization And Multi-Node Alignment</h2> <p>Policy per decision D-003:</p> <ul> <li>Canonical <code>timestamp_s</code> everywhere is epoch UTC from <code>time.time()</code> via the injected clock; no other time base appears in artifacts.</li> <li>Each process records its monotonic-vs-wall offset at start in metadata (detects wall-clock steps mid-run).</li> <li>Each node records NTP sync state in metadata when determinable.</li> <li>For multi-node runs, the controller bounds per-node clock offset with marker events: timestamp a no-op command on the remote node immediately before and after each remote stage; half the round trip bounds the offset. The bound is recorded in composite-bundle metadata.</li> <li>Reducers must flag (in measurement quality) any cross-node interval shorter than the recorded offset bound; such intervals are not used for energy attribution claims.</li> <li>Required precision: at 1-10 Hz power sampling, tens of milliseconds - comfortably within LAN NTP plus the marker bound.</li> </ul> <h2 id="controller-co-residency-controller-as-dut">Controller Co-Residency (Controller-As-DUT)</h2> <p>On Mac-local runs the controller process runs on the measured machine. Mitigation per decision D-013:</p> <ul> <li>The idle baseline is measured with the controller resident and quiescent, so the controller&#39;s floor load is included in what idle subtraction removes.</li> <li>During the measured window the controller only blocks on the runtime: no logging, no polling, no file writes; log records buffer in memory and flush after sampling stops.</li> <li>Residual risk is recorded, not hidden: OS background activity affects idle and measured windows alike; the upgrade path (remote-controlled Mac runs once the SSH transport exists) is queued as a validation comparison.</li> </ul> <h2 id="repetition-ordering-and-thermal-equilibrium">Repetition, Ordering, And Thermal Equilibrium</h2> <p>Per decisions D-005 and D-014:</p> <ul> <li>Each repetition is an independent run bundle; an experiment manifest groups members and records the executed order.</li> <li>Between live repetitions, cooldown v2 holds until the retained evidence has both a complete 30-second wall-clock span and at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code> of captured coverage (<code>coverage_fraction = 0.8</code> by default), and its duration-weighted idle-power mean satisfies the one-sided rule <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code> (10% by the production policy), while thermal pressure is Nominal. A below-reference mean therefore counts as recovery. An optional calibrated absolute ceiling is an additional upper cap and never an OR escape. The wait has a 5-minute cap; the cap is evaluated before release on every iteration, so recovery criteria first met at or after the deadline remain a <code>cap_hit</code> (with the late criteria recorded in the trace) and are recorded in the following repetition&#39;s measurement quality.</li> <li>The preceding baseline is eligible as a cooldown reference only when <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code>, all critical environment probes passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. An ineligible or unknown reference falls back to one frozen clean anchor: the NEG-8 reference start when present, otherwise the first admission-passing baseline. The anchor&#39;s source and hashes are recorded and it is never updated from later outcomes. With neither an eligible reference nor an anchor the gate fails closed. The following member records policy version, eligibility decision, anchor provenance, thresholds (including <code>coverage_fraction</code>), wall-clock span, required and observed coverage, thermal result, and the exact release criterion under <code>preceding_campaign_cooldown</code>. Historical recovered rows retain their recorded meaning and are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>Conditions are interleaved round-robin where model-reload cost permits; where blocks are operationally forced, the order is recorded so drift correlation can be audited (Phase 4 Stage 4.5 does this audit).</li> </ul> <h2 id="statistical-protocol">Statistical Protocol</h2> <p>Per decision D-014 (draft to be ratified against observed variance at Phase 4 Stage 4.0), amended 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3; amendments ratified by D-053):</p> <ul> <li>Repetitions: n &gt;= 5 for headline comparisons; n &gt;= 3 minimum elsewhere; the n is recorded per experiment.</li> <li>Intervals: report mean, sample standard deviation, and 95% confidence interval via Student t; Phase 4 runs a bootstrap sensitivity comparison and reports both where they materially disagree.</li> <li>Outliers: flagged by modified z-score on MAD &gt; 3.5; never silently dropped; reported with-and-without only when a physical cause is identified and documented; otherwise kept in headline numbers. Amendment 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3, ratified by D-053): at n &lt;= 10, reports also run a leave-one-out influence check on every claim-bearing contrast. The report lists the full-data estimate/CI/verdict and each leave-one-out estimate/CI/verdict. An omitted point is influential if it changes the sign, floor status, adjusted rejection/equivalence verdict, or moves the estimate by more than 0.25 x the active threshold: MDE for rank/MDE-gated claims, otherwise the floor gate. Influential points are reported as sensitivity evidence, not silently removed.</li> <li>Figures always show raw points alongside aggregates.</li> <li>Amendment 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3, ratified by D-053): differences are claimed from the confidence interval of the paired/block difference, or from the named model contrast, not by visual separation of marginal intervals. Where execution order was randomized, the analysis includes a permutation/randomization check for the same contrast following the actual randomization scheme, permuting labels only within exchangeable blocks/strata. The minimum for this check is 6 exchangeable blocks; below that count, report the check as not run and rely on the contrast CI with the caveat that randomization-inference sensitivity was underpowered. A paired contrast is preferred when it matches the design; mixed or hierarchical models are reserved for real dependence structures that a paired/block contrast cannot represent. Floor-gated outcomes use a three-way rule: below-floor contrasts are <code>not resolvable</code>; above-floor contrasts whose CI does not support direction are <code>unresolved</code> with no directional claim; equivalence or &quot;no difference&quot; language requires a predeclared equivalence gate whose margin exceeds the floor and whose contrast CI lies entirely within that margin.</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
docs/site/adapter_contracts.html:48:</code></pre> <p>Only the reducer may assign <code>below_floor</code>; <code>excluded_from_claim</code> is analysis-only and invalid in runtime events or summaries (D-045.4).</p> <p>Prompt-source handling is per item and mutually exclusive. <code>prompt_text</code> is encoded at generation time with adapter-normal special-token behavior (MLX uses <code>add_special_tokens=True</code>, so BOS is inside the planned prompt budget). <code>prompt_token_ids</code> is ids-native and delivered exactly as listed, with no BOS added; this is required for D-046 sentinel conditions. Absent text and ids use a synthetic prompt with <code>shape.planned_prompt_tokens</code>. Any field named <code>prompt_sha256</code> means the domain-separated token-ID hash, not a text hash.</p> <p>For prompt-text items with a SHA-256-shaped <code>source.source_sha256</code>, runtimes compare the realized prompt token-ID hash against <code>source_sha256</code>; if it does not match, they may accept <code>sha256(prompt_text)</code> as a text-domain manifest. Any other value fails the item closed as <code>malformed</code> with <code>status_reason: &quot;prompt_ids_mismatch&quot;</code>. For planned prompt token counts, <code>jw_mixed_v1</code> prompt-text items are budgeted and a realized/planned mismatch is fatal; affine ladder prompt-text items are nominal and receive an advisory annotation instead.</p> <p><code>suite_items.jsonl.prompt_source</code> is one of <code>prompt_text</code>, <code>token_ids</code>, or <code>synthetic</code>. <code>bos_present</code> records whether BOS is present in the realized prompt. For text-path adapters, when the tokenizer exposes a BOS id this is <code>add_special_tokens=True</code> and first realized id equals the tokenizer BOS id; when the tokenizer does not expose BOS identity, <code>bos_present</code> records the honest encode-mode proxy (<code>add_special_tokens=True</code>). Ids-native and synthetic suite prompts record <code>false</code> unless a future adapter explicitly materializes BOS as part of those sources.</p> <h2 id="telemetry-adapter">Telemetry Adapter</h2> <p>Telemetry answers how power and thermal state are measured.</p> <p>Required behavior:</p> <ul> <li>Report device metadata, including the rail manifest: the exact rail names whose per-timestamp sum defines the backend&#39;s canonical <code>power_w</code> (D-018). Rail manifest entries are strings; non-string entries are rejected by the bundle reader rather than coerced.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Start power sampling.</li> <li>Stop power sampling.</li> <li>Emit raw power samples.</li> <li>Report thermal state when available.</li> <li>Return structured failure if telemetry permission is missing.</li> </ul> <p>Rail-row timestamp contract (D-027, Slice 2N.4): one sample instant is one clock read, fanned out to one row per manifest rail, all carrying that instant&#39;s single <code>timestamp_s</code>. A manifest rail may appear at most once for a given timestamp; duplicate <code>(timestamp_s, rail)</code> rows are invalid, including single-rail manifests. With a multi-rail manifest, a timestamp carrying only a subset of the manifest rails is a misalignment: the shared bundle reader raises a structured failure (the reducer reports FAILED; the report omits the chart) and default bundle validation reports the same trace-policy problem rather than silently producing an interleaved, undersummed, or double-counted curve. An adapter whose hardware samples rails at genuinely different instants must resample/align to shared timestamps before emitting rows - alignment policy belongs to the adapter that knows its hardware.</p> <p>Powermetrics NUL-framed plist parsing is lenient only for the final unparseable frame, and only after at least one complete frame parsed successfully. The adapter preserves the raw plist verbatim, drops that final frame only from derived parsing (<code>power_trace.csv</code> and rich telemetry), and records a non-gating <code>metadata.device.parse_diagnostics[]</code> entry describing the dropped tail. A midstream unparseable frame, or a capture with no complete frames, is still a hard parse failure.</p> <p>Mock telemetry sampling convention (D-019): for any nonzero <code>start_sampling</code>/<code>stop_sampling</code> span, <code>MockTelemetryAdapter</code> stamps synthetic measured samples strictly inside that adapter span, never at the boundary clock reads. It uses a centered nominal-period grid at the configured <code>sampling.power_hz</code>; if that would produce fewer than two samples, it emits two evenly spaced interior samples instead. This preserves deterministic constant-power math while ensuring the controller&#39;s post-start/pre-stop measured markers contain enough samples for reducer integration under both fake and real clocks.</p> <p>Initial telemetry backends:</p> <ul> <li><code>mock</code></li> <li><code>powermetrics</code></li> <li><code>nvidia_smi</code></li> <li><code>jetson_rails</code></li> <li><code>wall_meter</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="idle-admission-core-policy-extension-t0-5-audit-p1-1-p1-2-additive">Idle-Admission Core Policy Extension (T0.5, audit P1.1/P1.2; additive)</h2> <p>GPU-idle-only admission is no longer sufficient. The pure evaluators in <code>joulewise/idle_admission.py</code> add three fail-closed surfaces, driven by an additive campaign-policy sidecar section keyed <code>idle_admission_extension</code> (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_extension.v1</code>):</p> <ul> <li><p><strong>CPU-aware idle admission</strong>: policy-configurable criteria over the pre-run baseline rich telemetry (<code>rich_telemetry_idle.jsonl</code>) - nearest-rank p95 of the per-record max per-CPU busy ratio (<code>1 - idle_ratio - down_ratio</code>, clamped, so parked CPUs never read as busy) against <code>cpu_criteria.cpu_busy_ratio_p95_max</code>, and p95 of <code>processor_combined_power_w</code> against <code>cpu_criteria.processor_combined_power_w_p95_max</code>, with at least <code>cpu_criteria.min_samples</code> records. Admission requires the existing GPU-idle admission AND these criteria. Missing, malformed, or insufficient telemetry FAILS CLOSED when <code>cpu_criteria.on_missing_telemetry</code> is <code>fail</code> (mandatory for a production profile); an exploratory policy may use <code>flag</code> but must set <code>claim_bearing: false</code> (explicitly non-claim-bearing).</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Adapter-wattage continuity</strong>: <code>collect_environment_guard_observation</code> records the adapter surface (<code>power.adapter_watts</code>, <code>power.adapter_description</code>, plus a normalized <code>adapter_power_observation</code>) per admission observation when called with <code>include_adapter_power=True</code> (default off so pre-hookup callers keep their exact probe sequence AND their exact observation shape; the controller hookup opts in). Under the default flag the <code>power</code> block and <code>adapter_power_observation</code> keys are ABSENT entirely - not present as all-None placeholders - so the verdict&#39;s continuity scan (which treats any guard observation carrying a <code>power</code> key as an adapter observation) never ingests unverifiable unknown-wattage placeholders from callers that did not opt in. The campaign verdict evaluates the ordered observation sequence: wattage discontinuities (the live 140-&gt;70-&gt;140 W negotiation precedent) and description/power-source changes are NAMED conditions - recorded data, never a silent pass and never an implicit abort. Unknown adapter wattage fails closed when <code>adapter_wattage.require_known_wattage</code> is true (mandatory for production); stable known wattage passes.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Prospective NEG-8 SCREEN + BUDGET</strong> — <strong>Ed-ratified 2026-07-24, superseding the prior gross-only amendment:</strong> the screen is claim-family aligned. It independently gates gross and idle-subtracted point drift against distinct bounds derived from the same named, settled, same-condition <code>n &gt;= 10</code> corpus. The hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact records both families. For legacy one-member endpoints, <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> remains <code>max(sample_range_j, t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2))</code>. Prospective endpoints are three members each: the screen uses the start/end endpoint means, records their standard errors, and compares the absolute mean delta (not a second SEM-inflated margin) to <code>max(mean(largest_3)-mean(smallest_3), t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2/3))</code>. The extreme-triplet term retains the largest corpus-supported endpoint-mean contrast; the Student-t term predicts two new three-member endpoint means. Recording SEM without adding it again avoids double-counting repeatability already represented by the bound. Gross envelope corners remain diagnostics only.</p> <p>Every evaluated window also mints a strictly positive allowance per family: <code>max(max(start_mean,midpoint,end_mean)-min(...), derived_bound)</code>. One midpoint member is mandatory for the prospective 3+1+3 protocol, so a non-monotone interior excursion cannot disappear behind similar endpoints. No duration multiplier is applied: the settled corpus identifies repeatability, not a drift-per-time law, and inventing linear physics would be less defensible than the observed trajectory maximum. The verdict records the no-scaling decision, member counts/means/SEMs, midpoint, excursion, selected bound, allowance, and derivation hash. Floor records add the family-matched allowance after the guarded/corner-widened floor; validation recomputes the sum and claim consumption uses both the drift-widened floor and the named deterministic allowance term.</p> <p>Missing/invalid family evidence refuses distinctly: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (gross) and <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code> (idle-subtracted); both spellings are Ed-ratified D-078 registry additions. Family failures retain <code>neg8_bracket_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for gross and add <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for idle-subtracted. A delta exactly on its bound passes. The v1 sidecar&#39;s <code>max_abs_delta_j</code>/<code>max_rel_delta</code> remain legacy transport fields and do not gate amended rows.</p> <p><strong>BOUND FRESHNESS addendum — Ed-ratified 2026-07-24:</strong> the same sealed artifact carries <code>freshness.derived_at_s</code>, a fixed 24-hour <code>max_age_s = 86400</code>, and exact OS-build, power-supply-identity, and calibration-artifact-identity bindings. Twenty-four hours mirrors the governed instrument-calibration horizon: it permits one controlled measurement day without treating repeatability as indefinitely transferable. Evaluation records its timestamp, expiry, artifact and observed bindings, binding-resolution status, and every triggered re-derivation reason. Horizon expiry, OS build change, power-supply change, calibration identity change, or unresolved current binding makes both family bounds stale and refuses with the registered <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code>. A v1 artifact with an authentic pre-addendum seal but no freshness block is replay-readable only to produce that stale refusal; it is never grandfathered. Malformed or unsealed artifacts remain underived under the two family-specific spellings. The superseded pre-SCREEN+BUDGET gross-only v1 shape (no <code>claim_family_bounds</code>) is not replayable and refuses as malformed/underived; &quot;pre-addendum replay&quot; applies only to the dual-family shape with <code>claim_family_bounds</code> present and freshness absent.</p> <p>The bracket is a WHOLE-WINDOW check: the evaluated basis must contain both endpoints. Legacy pair-only windows (a5-a8) remain evaluable as 1+0+1: both families screen and each allowance is <code>max(abs(delta), bound)</code>. Replicated endpoints plus midpoint apply prospectively; existing basis-scoped legacy verdict rows retain their frozen interpretation. Per-segment invocations with only one endpoint (or neither) record <code>neg8_bracket_not_evaluated</code>, never a spurious missing/failure. A reference genuinely absent from an explicit whole-window pass still fails closed.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Verdict surface: <code>scripts/run_campaign.py</code> records the additive <code>idle_admission_core</code> section (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_core_verdict.v1</code>) on the campaign verdict with per-member CPU-admission results, the continuity result, the bracket result, and the union of named conditions. A sidecar without the extension yields the named condition <code>idle_admission_extension_unconfigured</code>.</p> <p>Hash/version enforcement: the campaign policy binding hash is the sha256 of the full sidecar bytes, extension included - changing any new field changes the policy identity; the extension additionally records its own canonical-JSON sha256 and requires exact schema/policy version strings and exact keys (unknown or missing keys are rejected).</p> <p>Deployment note (C2 hookup complete): <code>CampaignPolicy.from_mapping</code> now owns the typed additive extension parse, including profile-dependent fail-closed validation, so controller child runs re-parse the full hash-bound sidecar without a runner-side strip/parse workaround. The tracked production and exploratory sidecars carry the extension. During each live admission attempt, the powermetrics adapter exposes that attempt&#39;s rich CPU records in memory; the controller evaluates CPU/combined-power criteria before workload invoke, records the result in the existing <code>environment_admission.attempts</code> ledger, and retries/aborts or flags according to the base policy. Attempt selection is explicit, so the final admission decision and final CPU telemetry cannot be paired across retries. Current-mint attempt rows bind each measurement to a finite <code>start_s</code>/<code>end_s</code> wall-clock (epoch) window; the ordered ledger must be strictly increasing and non-overlapping (<code>end_i &lt;= start_(i+1)</code>). Missing or malformed timing refuses current claims, while frozen replay semantics remain unchanged. Because the windows are wall-clock, a backwards clock step between attempts mints an out-of-order ledger that strict validation permanently refuses — a fail-closed false refusal, never an admission; re-run the campaign member if this occurs. Missing adapter telemetry fails closed on live clocks; <code>FakeClock</code> fixture runs retain the pre-hookup GPU decision and record <code>cpu_admission_enforced: false</code> alongside the named missing-telemetry result. That field is an unconditional claim barrier in reducers/extraction; it is never evidence that GPU-only admission was scientifically sufficient. Live guard observations opt in to adapter-power capture, including a mandatory post-workload observation for every member. A missing post sample is unknown wattage (and therefore a production refusal), so renegotiation during the final workload cannot be hidden by an earlier clean sample.</p> <p>At window end, chain scripts can run:</p> <pre><code class="language-sh">python3 scripts/run_campaign.py --whole-window-verdict \
docs/site/adapter_contracts.html:51:</code></pre> <p>This resolves finalized members from the matching campaign provenance ledger (falling back to a diagnostic-only scan that cannot pass when membership is unbound), applies ordinary strict bundle validation, appends an <code>idle_admission_whole_window_verdict</code> row to the campaign log, and evaluates NEG-8 in explicit whole-window mode. The dual-family bound artifact is minted separately with:</p> <pre><code class="language-sh">python3 scripts/run_campaign.py --derive-neg8-drift-bound SETTLED_CORPUS.json \

GATE: Ed ratifies the amendment first — do not soften the gate in code before ratification.</p></details> <span class="source-chip" title="TASK_QUEUE.md · commit de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span> </div> </article><article class="lane-card" data-lane="AGENT"> <div class="priority-band p1"></div> <div class="lane-main"> <div class="lane-head"><span class="lane-rank mono">#A46</span><span class="mono task-code">FLOOR-WORKLOAD-SIZING-01</span><span class="status-chip">READY</span><span class="lane-chip lane-agent">AGENT</span></div> <p class="status-note">READY</p> <h2>Re-size the floor/science campaign workloads so measured effects clear the duration-independent attribution floor, and pilot the resulting effect-to-floor ratio before spending quiet-machine nights on ABBA collection at current sizes.</h2> <details><summary>Acceptance</summary><p>Anchor-attribution error is approximately duration-independent (~1 J regardless of phase size) while effects scale with workload, so lengthening prefill/decode raises effect-to-floor linearly at zero instrument cost.
